title: Introduce federated KMS scope validator and audit-sample-rate-preserver
author: Priya Nair
ci_status: pass (flake rerun required on integration, green after retry)
description: Context: Customers operating in multiple regions run into two compliance gaps: (1) operator/service principals being able to request KMS keys outside their allowed scope when KMS provider mappings are federated, and (2) audit logs losing fidelity due to aggressive sample-rate throttling in high-throughput ingestion paths. This PR implements a federated KMS scope validator that enforces provider-level and region-level key scoping for tenant and operator claims, integrates the validator into RBAC v2 decision flow, and adds an audit-sample-rate-preserver that ensures compliance-sensitive events (key operations, residency-denied attempts, role-grants) are preserved even under sampling. What changed: 1) new crate authz/validator/federated_kms.rs — stateless validator that evaluates claimed_kms_provider + requested_key_region against tenant-affinities and operator-allowed-scopes; supports multiple provider aliases and fallback mappings. 2) RBAC v2 hook integration — validator is called during the pre-authorize hook; on mismatch returns explicit DENY with structured audit reason. 3) Audit pipeline change — sampler now accepts a preserve-list of event categories and a budgeted-preserve algorithm to guarantee N preserved events per minute per-tenant while keeping global ingestion bounds. 4) Migration shim — backwards-compatible feature-flag to enable validator in shadow (audit-only) mode for 2 weeks before full enforcement. 5) Tests and docs — unit + integration tests covering provider aliasing, operator-scope inheritance, cross-tenant attempt simulation, and sampler preserve guarantees; security runbook and operator-config docs added. Design notes & motivation: In federated KMS setups (multi-cloud / partner providers) a naive provider mapping can allow an operator scoped to region A to implicitly use a provider alias that routes to region B. The validator uses a compact policy matrix (tenant_affinity + operator_claims -> allowed_providers/regions) and short-circuits to a safe deny rather than attempting transparent remapping. The audit preserver addresses the real-world observation that high-throughput tenants had their KMS-deny events dropped by the previous uniform sampler, making post-incident forensics unreliable. Rollout plan: - Stage 1 (shadow mode): enable via feature flag (authz.kms_validator.mode=shadow) for 14 days; collect metrics (validator.denies.shadow_count, preserved_events.count). - Stage 2 (canary deny): enable for 5% of tenants selected by pattern for 48 hours, review denies, false-positive rate. - Stage 3 (global enforcement): flip to enforce after remediation window. Backwards compatibility & safety: Default mode is shadow; no change to existing policies until explicitly enabled. The preserve sampler is opt-in per-tenant via audit.config.preserve_categories with safe defaults for newly created organizations. Testing performed: - Unit tests for alias resolution and policy matrix (100% coverage for new validator module). - Integration tests wiring validator into RBAC v2 decision flow. - Load test for audit pipeline ensuring preserved event budgets do not exceed ingestion caps. - Purple-team runbook exercise simulating cross-region KMS request and verifying audit sequence. Checklist: [x] Code + unit tests added [x] Integration tests added [x] Docs and runbook updated [x] Feature flag added (shadow mode) [x] Perf/bench numbers attached [x] Security review done (Olivia Chen) Related: ENG-4892 (policy matrix), PM-774 (compliance roadmap), SUP-1427 (customer support ticket showing leaked key-usage telemetry).

review_comments: Olivia Chen: Can we add a short-circuit deny metric (validator.denies.enforced) and include the reason code so SRE alerts can be tuned?
Priya Nair: Added validator.denies.enforced and reason_code tag; increment only on non-shadow denies. Also added docs to explain alert thresholds.
Marcus Lee: Unit test looks good. Integration test fails intermittently in CI due to timing in the sampler budget reset — suggest deterministic clock injection.

Diego Alvarez: Security review - ensure the validator cannot be used to enumerate tenant affinities by probing response timings. Recommend constant-time path for alias lookup.

ci_notes: Initial CI had an integration flake around sampler timing; fixed by deterministic test_clock. All checks green after re-run (unit, integration, lint, fmt, cargo-audit).
release_notes: Added a federated KMS scope validator integrated into RBAC v2 (shadow mode by default) and an audit-sample-rate-preserver to guarantee preservation of compliance-sensitive events under sampling. Feature gated; operators should review runbook before enabling enforcement.
security_impact_summary: Improves enforcement of key-region/provider scoping and increases audit fidelity for KMS-related events. Default behavior is non-breaking (shadow) but rollout to enforce mode must be coordinated with customers using federated provider aliases.
observability_changes: New metrics: validator.denies.shadow_count, validator.denies.enforced, validator.latency_ms, audit.preserved_events.count; dashboards and alert rules updated in docs and ops runbook.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag authz.kms_validator.mode can be set to 'shadow', 'canary', 'enforce'. Use audit.config.preserve_categories to opt tenants into preserved budgets. See ops/runbooks/security/kms-validator-playbook.md for rollback steps.
misc: This PR is intentionally conservative: shadow mode for two weeks, explicit canary selection, and an opt-in preserve sampler per-tenant. The validator policy matrix is intentionally small and pluggable for future policy compilers.
